contracts.web: src/core/pulsarPanHold.ts: press = one immediate tick, then a 100 ms browser interval of pulsarPanTick using the stored step; a press while held keeps the single running timer. WEB lifecycle: stops on primary pointer up, pointer cancel, capture loss, window blur, page hidden, inactive host, committed load, modal open (tick refused) and unmount; the click that follows a pointer press does not step again. Keyboard/assistive activation (Enter/Space) steps once per physical press: auto-repeated keydowns are ignored and no timer starts; held keys are forgotten on window blur, a hidden page, an inactive host, a load and a modal, because their keyup may never reach the button; the native buttons cannot be keyboard-panned. A tick whose redraw Number cannot represent is refused ('display-unsupported'), which stops the hold. Browser interval cadence vs Windows WM_TIMER resolution/coalescing is not claimed equal. |window| ≤ 1e12 s.

contracts.web: Number, not x87 Extended: an admitted tiny nonzero gain (for example 1e-320) can make the quotient overflow to ±Infinity where Extended stays finite. Such a placement is refused with a visible 'number-unsupported' status; the previous cursor, readout and measurement and the loaded bytes are kept, and a refused MouseUp creates no pending entry. A later accepted placement replaces the refusal status. No zero substitution, no lower gain limit and no reordered arithmetic is introduced.

contracts.observed: Called after the panel's axis/trace repaint. For each stored time not below Single 0x56c440 (vertical +0xc, reference +0x16; jb skips at 0x56c374/0x56c3b7): x = Round((t − start)·zoom/dt), then 0x56c448 recomputes t from x (re-quantization) and draws only when x ≥ 0. Horizontal value +0x20 not below 0x56c440 (jb 0x56c3fa): y = Round(base[ch] − v·100·gain·factor), then 0x56c6dc without recomputing the value; it draws and stores only for 0 ≤ y < base[ch]. A skipped or rejected cursor is not drawn on the repainted panel, and its stored pixel, value and readout are not rewritten.
contracts.staticData: Single 0x56c440 decodes directly to 0.0 (coordinator static data decode, COORDINATOR-correction-triage/static-data-decode.json). Static evidence only: it does not establish runtime FPU comparison or rounding parity
contracts.web: Each panel cursor carries verticalVisible/referenceVisible/horizontalVisible. A placement sets it (x ≥ 0, or an accepted y), so a negative time or value is drawn right after a manual click. A redraw that skips the entry or rejects its y clears it, keeping the stored pixel, time/value, readout and measurement; a later redraw with a valid projection draws it again. A vertical or reference line is drawn only on a client pixel 0 ≤ x < 400. Keyboard arrows step from a line drawn there; otherwise they use a fixed web edge origin (pixel 0, or row base − 1 for the horizontal cursor). WEB Number boundary: a projection that is not finite in Number (for example v·100 overflowing before gain and factor bring it back, where Extended would not overflow) is not attributed to the native out-of-range rejection. The whole zoom, pan, pan tick or factor change is refused with 'display-unsupported' and changes nothing: no partial re-quantization, no hidden line, the same display, cursors and measurement. The arithmetic order is kept; no gain floor or zero is introduced, and no x87 equivalence is claimed.

contracts.observed: MouseDown: left sets drag flag 0x5dd and places the own cursor by mode 0x57c+ch (0 vertical, 1 horizontal); right sets 0x5dc and places the reference cursor on all three panels. MouseMove acts only with ssLeft (0x08) / ssRight (0x10) while the matching flag is set. MouseUp: clears the flag after the final placement, then 0x57f+ch := IsEmpty || highest < ch; when that is false, Record (+0x464) is enabled.
contracts.web: x,y are clamped to integer client pixels [0,399]×[0,Height[ch]−1]; the native code can receive captured coordinates outside the panel. A WEB toggle maps the primary button/touch to the reference cursor; keyboard arrows act as one click per press. WEB boundary: pointer cancel, lost pointer capture and host deactivation clear both drag latches (pulsarPointerRelease). This is not a native MouseUp: no cursor is placed and no panel becomes pending; cursors, measurement and confirmed list are kept. WEB pointer ownership: only the primary pointer whose press set a latch drives the shared latches; non-primary pointers and other pointers' cancel or capture loss are ignored, so a secondary cancellation does not end the primary drag. Native left/right handling is unchanged and no multi-touch behavior is modelled. WEB Number boundary: a MouseUp whose own placement is refused ('number-unsupported') does not change that panel's pending flag or Record; a y rejected by 0x56c6dc is the native rule and still marks the panel pending

contracts.inference: nativeLineCandidate follows the decoded literals but is not a file-writer contract: the CSV writer is gated and number text is not x87 parity. It is an opaque internal candidate, not a validatable or exportable CSV: the object and file names are wrapped in '"' without escaping, so an admitted name containing '"' or ',' makes the field boundaries ambiguous. contracts.web: Comments: printable ASCII without '"', ≤ 80 characters (compiled Cmnt1Ed.MaxLength; the native shortstring storage capacity81 is distinct). The list lives only in this tab; a visible note says it is not part of Save investigation and is discarded on refresh/close. The record and clear prompts are native <dialog> elements opened with showModal() (browser top layer: inert page, contained focus, topmost modal wins); Tab/Shift+Tab wrap via a keydown handler on the dialog element only, never a page-level trap. Escape is Cancel/No, the default button is Cancel/No and focus returns to Record or Clear. A dialog opens only while the panel is active and rendered and no other dialog is open; an inactive panel closes it and keeps the record session (draft included) or clear stage for reentry. This is web behavior, not VCL modal parity

numericPolicy: Metadata and samples are IEEE doubles from Number(lexeme). Native metadata is x87 Extended and samples are Double after an Extended parse. Round() = roundNearestEven (src/core/numericPolicy.ts), not a measured x87 control word. No x87 parity is claimed. A cursor value or record field that is not finite in Number is refused ('number-unsupported'), never stored, formatted as blank or recorded, and a refused MouseUp marks nothing pending. A redraw projection that is not finite in Number refuses the whole display change ('display-unsupported') instead of hiding the line. Operation order is never rearranged to avoid an overflow.
